original_poem:
आकाशाचा पाय  
खोलातुन आवाज येतो,  
आभाळाच्या काठावर,  
धरणा धरून उभा आहे,  
आसमानातच आहे माणूस.
translated_poem:
Feet of the sky,  
A voice rises from deep,  
On the edge of the heavens,  
Standing firm,  
Humans dwell in the sky.

stanzas.loss_note: धरणा धरून (dharaṇā dharūn) means 'staging a sit-in protest / holding firm in stubborn demand', a phrase with strong social-protest resonance in Marathi; the translation 'standing firm' loses this connotation of desperate, defiant supplication.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the unreachable foundation on which human existence precariously rests
a cry of existential anguish rising from the depths of human helplessness
the threshold between mortal limitation and infinite aspiration
humanity's stubborn, protest-like insistence on meaning at the edge of the void

cultural_entities.translation_note: Dharaṇā is a specifically Marathi/Indian form of protest-sit-in, carrying connotations of collective social defiance; 'standing firm' in the translation erases this activist register.
